To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cloud storage services generate a significant amount of unnecessary traffic due to session maintenance, and UDS can significantly reduce the amount of this unnecessary traffic while maintaining rapid synchronization.

1) cloud storage applications often generate session maintenance traffic orders of magnitude higher than the useful update traffic; 2) UDS significantly reduces session maintenance traffic and improves the overall performance of cloud storage services; and 3) UDS can be implemented with minimal changes to existing cloud storage applications, and can be further enhanced with a simple kernel modification.
the traffic overuse phenomenon exists in cloud storage services, and we have developed a mechanism, UDS, to address this problem.

the design, implementation and evaluation of a new synchronization mechanism for cloud storage services that significantly reduces network overhead, while maintaining the responsiveness that users expect from such services.
the problem of efficiently synchronizing large numbers of small files in the context of cloud storage services, and we present a novel approach to address this problem.
the design and implementation of a novel middleware that improves the network efficiency of Dropbox-like cloud storage services.

UDS is an efficient and effective mechanism to improve the performance of cloud-based storage services.
our proposed mechanism, UDS, can significantly reduce the network overhead of cloud storage applications, while also improving their CPU efficiency.
we propose a novel solution to the traffic overuse issue, which is a significant source of inefficiency in cloud storage services.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified the traffic overuse phenomenon in Dropbox-like cloud storage services, and proposed the update-batched synchronization (UDS), a novel and efficient synchronization mechanism that can reduce the traffic generated by such services by up to 90% and improve the synchronization performance by 2.5 times.
UDS reduces the network traffic generated in a cloud storage service by up to 90%, and the CPU utilization by up to 50%.
, in the presence of short, frequent updates, cloud storage applications generate a large amount of unnecessary network traffic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the traffic overuse behavior in cloud storage applications can be effectively addressed with a simple and lightweight solution.
cloud storage services are not as efficient as they should be, and that there are simple and effective ways to make them much more efficient.
, by batching update traffic from users, we can achieve a significant improvement in both the bandwidth and CPU efficiency of cloud storage applications.
